summary: Staggered credential rollout triggering unexpected 429s for webhook orchestrator
description:
Issue summary: Customer FleetPush reports a persistent spike of 429 responses across multiple webhook endpoints after a credential rotation they initiated. Impact: ~30% of webhook deliveries return 429s for ~10-30 minutes per rotation wave, causing backfill and duplicate deliveries on their side. Environment: production (dedicated pool) in us-west-2.

Observed behavior:
- FleetPush triggered a staged API credential rotation via our Console (rollout window: 03/10 02:00 UTC) with rapid overlapping activation waves from their CI.
- During and shortly after activation waves we see tenant-wide 429s on webhook routes and increased token-accounting events in rate-limiter logs.
- The customer uses a webhook orchestrator that opens many short-lived connections (HTTP/2 multiplexed clients) and aggressively retries.

Expected behavior:
- Staged credential rotations should not cause tenant-level token exhaustion or unexpected 429s for existing active sessions.

Notes: Customer believes rotation UI toggles were staggered locally but orchestration triggered near-simultaneous activation in our edge fleet due to webhook CI concurrency.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) In dedicated pool, initiate credential rotation from console for tenant with multiplexed webhook clients.
2) Simulate webhook orchestrator starting 200 short-lived HTTP/2 streams that authenticate with the new credential at once.
3) Observe 429 rates on /v1/webhook/* routes and token-accounting increments in rate-limiter logs for the tenant.
4) Replay with staggered activation (1s to 60s jitter) to compare behavior.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:03:12Z RATE-LIMITER tenant=fp-23 event=token_grant delta=+200 window=1s source=edge-proxy-12
2026-03-10T02:03:15Z EDGE proxy=edge-proxy-12 trace=trc-9a7 auth=new-cred-abc status=429 path=/v1/webhook/push
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: simultaneous activation across many edge proxies led to transient double-counting (preflight + activation) against the tenant burst pool. Correlated spike with user-initiated rotation window and high fanout from webhook orchestrator.
Actions taken:
- Pulled rate-limiter token accounting for tenant across edges; saw sharp refill / issue windows matching customer's activation timestamps.
- Replayed activation in staging with local orchestrator: reproduces elevated 429 when activation requests are batched within the same refill epoch.
- Confirmed that health-check and preflight probes from orchestrator contributed to accounting.
Pending: SRE to review edge-proxy activation path that increments token windows on credential handshake and preflight simultaneously.
comments: 2026-03-10 04:12 - Support (Maya Chen): Investigating after customer ticket. They've provided request IDs and a short trace. Asked for exact rotation schedule and client retry policy.

2026-03-10 05:03 - Customer (Alexei Petrov, FleetPush): We triggered rotation in 6 waves from CI; believed waves were staggered but orchestrator starts many workers which all attempt new auth within ~20s windows. We've attached our webhook delivery logs.

2026-03-10 08:40 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Correlated tenant token events with edge logs. Observed multiple activation RPCs and preflight checks counted as separate grants. Proposed short-term mitigation: recommend customer enable client-side jitter (>=30s) and Service to apply a 45s smoothing window for credential activation accounting on dedicated pools.

2026-03-11 09:17 - Eng (Priya Das): Technical note: edge-proxy currently records activation event and preflight as distinct token events because handshake occurs before token binding completes. Will prototype idempotent activation dedupe for simultaneous activations by the same tenant key across a 60s window.
2026-03-12 10:02 - Support (Maya Chen): Shared mitigation steps with customer and scheduled a maintenance window to test smoothing on a small subset of the customer's routes next week.
resolution:
Mitigation recommended and partially applied: 1) Customer changed orchestrator to add 45s random jitter to credential activation attempts; 2) Ops enabled a 45s activation smoothing flag for the customer's dedicated pool (canary on 10% of edge-ips). Early results show 86% drop in 429 spikes during rotation waves. Root cause: activation + preflight were double-accounted into the tenant burst window during rapid, overlapping activations.
Follow-ups: implement server-side dedupe for activation events (ENG-4578), update rotation runbook with recommended jitter and console UX to surface activation smoothing option, and add metric alarm to surface multi-edge activation spikes.
